results.title: Poddle: Swing your phone, play pickleball on any computer! | Product Hunt
results.content:
To move around the court, your webcam tracks where you stand. The video never leaves your computer. No camera? The game runs you to the ball automatically, like Wii Sports tennis, so you just swing.  
  
Early into the project, I added phone support for ease of testing. It ended up staying, though, since everyone already has one, and the time to play was so much faster than AirPods.  
  
You can also play Matt the bot at various difficulties, play friends online, earn trophies, run a knockout tournament, or watch live matches.  
  
Poddle is free, and you don't need an account unless you’re someone who likes progression and tracking your stats. Any feedback on how the swing feels and on potential future features is greatly appreciated. Have fun! 🥒 [...] Play now:   
How to play:   
  
P.S. See if you're one of the players who can beat Matt on Pro difficulty 😈 [...] ### Top forum threads

What do you think? …

Daniel

Hey Product Hunt, I'm Daniel, and this is my first launch! 😁  
  
Poddle started as a last-minute hackathon idea. AirPods have motion sensors, so we wondered if one could work as a pickleball paddle, in Wii Sports fashion. And it worked better than we expected! We didn't win anything, but I kept building it anyway out of love for the idea of the project, and I've been having tons of fun with my friends at university clubs playing and testing it ever since.  
  
Most of my time went into making the swing feel right. A motion sensor knows how your hand turns, not where it is, so the game reads the swing itself: speed and reach set the power, direction aims it, a scoop lobs it, and a wrist cut adds spin.

results.content:
Title: Improve Pickleball Grip for Better Play – Swinton Pickleball
# Troubleshooting Grip Issues With Your Pickleball Paddle. Your grip on a pickleball paddle plays a bigger part in your game than you might think. When the handle doesn’t feel quite right in your hand, even the best paddle won’t make up for the lack of control. Whether your hand keeps slipping, your fingers start to cramp, or the grip just feels off, it can throw your rhythm out of balance and make games more frustrating than fun. Many players, both new and experienced, run into issues with how their paddle feels after extended use or during certain weather conditions. Grip problems don’t always mean you need a new paddle. Addressing grip comfort and function can help your hand feel more relaxed, give you a steadier hold, and cut down on mis-hits. By figuring out what’s going wrong and making a few tweaks, you’ll be able to focus more on your game and less on constantly readjusting your hands. Before making changes, it helps to know exactly what kind of grip issue you're dealing with. **- Discomfort:** The grip feels too thin, too thick, or digs into your fingers. **- Blistering or fatigue:** You may find your hand sore after short matches due to rough grip texture or lack of padding. **- Imbalanced feeling:** When your paddle feels heavier on one side, the issue might come from uneven grip wear or a poor grip wrap. These issues can impact how well you swing, control the ball, and even your reaction time. If you notice you're adjusting your grip often or your shots don't have the same accuracy or force they used to, your paddle may need some attention. One of the most common complaints players have is that their hand slips on the paddle handle. This can make it hard to stay in control of your paddle. If your grip size doesn’t match your hand or if the material’s too rough, you’re probably going to feel it pretty fast. The good news is that making your grip feel better doesn’t take a ton of effort—just a few small changes based on what you need.
